title: Onboarding email copy v1 (Lifecycle Growth Sprint) — 5-email series
body:
Doc purpose
- Draft copy for 5-email onboarding sequence (self-serve / PLG developers)
- Includes subject line variants, preview text, and CTA links (with UTMs)
- Includes open questions + review comments

Primary goal
- Activation: first successful production-like inference call (first 2xx completion) within 24h/72h.
Secondary goals
- Encourage streaming success, dashboard views (latency/cost), and next milestones (billing added, higher usage, route/deployment created, invite teammate).

Audience + triggers (v1 assumptions — confirm in PM-413)
- Audience: new self-serve signups (workspace created) who have not reached activation milestone.
- Suppressions:
  - If user unsubscribed or global marketing opt-out.
  - If user is on sales-assisted sequence (Sales/CS owns) OR marked “do_not_email_onboarding”.
  - If user reaches activation (first_request_success) before a given email, suppress subsequent “getting started” emails and switch to “next steps” only (Email #5).
- Personalization tokens (Marketo/Customer.io style placeholders; adjust to tooling):
  - {{first_name}} (fallback: “there”)
  - {{workspace_name}}
  - {{api_key_create_url}} (deep link to Console)
  - {{quickstart_url}} (language-specific when known)
  - {{docs_troubleshooting_url}}
  - {{console_dashboard_url}}
  - {{unsub_url}}

Link + UTM conventions (Tyler to confirm final naming)
- Base UTM proposal for this sequence:
  - utm_source=customerio (or marke-to; TBD)
  - utm_medium=email
  - utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1
  - utm_content={{email_id}}_{{variant}}
  - utm_term={{segment}} (optional)
- NOTE: All console deep links should preserve UTM params on redirect (ENG-2844 / PR_8944).

Tone guidelines (from onboarding messaging pillars)
- Developer-first, practical, minimal hype.
- Lead with “get to first success fast,” then performance economics (latency/cost/reliability).
- Avoid absolute claims (e.g., “fastest”, “guaranteed”). If we reference benchmarks, link to substantiation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
EMAIL #1 — Welcome + quickstart (send: ~10 min after signup)
Email ID: E1_welcome
Goal: Get them to create API key and make first request (curl/SDK). Reduce time-to-first-success.
Segment: New signup, api_key_created = false OR first_request_success = false.

Subject line variants
- A: “Your Redwood API key + a 60-second first request”
- B: “Ship your first inference call (copy/paste)”
- C (optional): “Redwood quickstart: first response in minutes”

Preview text variants
- A: “Create a key, run one curl command, and you’re live.”
- B: “Copy/paste example + troubleshooting for common 401/403.”

Body (v1)
Hi {{first_name}},

Welcome to Redwood Inference. Here’s the fastest path to a first successful call:

1) Create an API key
Create a key for {{workspace_name}} here:
{{api_key_create_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E1_welcome_{{variant}}

2) Make your first request (copy/paste)
Curl (works everywhere):
- Quickstart: {{quickstart_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E1_welcome_{{variant}}

If you prefer an SDK:
- TypeScript: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/sdk/typescript/quickstart?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E1_welcome_{{variant}}
- Python: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/sdk/python/quickstart?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E1_welcome_{{variant}}

Common blockers (quick fixes)
- 401/403: check the key + workspace, and verify env var is set
- 404 model: pick a model from the catalog in Console
- Timeouts: start with a shorter max_tokens and enable streaming (we’ll cover next)

CTA (primary)
- “Create API key” -> {{api_key_create_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E1_welcome_{{variant}}
CTA (secondary)
- “Open quickstart” -> {{quickstart_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E1_welcome_{{variant}}

Footer line
If you didn’t sign up for Redwood, you can ignore this email. Unsubscribe: {{unsub_url}}

Review comments / notes
- Soojin: keep “60-second” claim unless we’re confident; maybe “a minute or two”
- Henry: confirm whether we want to mention “first 2xx completion” explicitly anywhere (probably no; internal)
- Dev: include a direct link to troubleshooting for auth errors

--------------------------------------------------------------------
EMAIL #2 — First success check-in + troubleshooting (send: +4 hours if not activated)
Email ID: E2_first_success
Goal: recover folks stuck on auth/model selection; move to first_request_success.
Trigger: first_request_success = false.

Subject line variants
- A: “Stuck on your first request? 3 quick fixes”
- B: “Common setup errors (and how to fix them fast)”

Preview text variants
- A: “Most first-day issues are keys, model IDs, or timeouts.”
- B: “We put the top fixes in one place—plus a known-good curl.”

Body (v1)
Hi {{first_name}},

If you haven’t gotten a successful response yet, you’re not alone—most first-day issues fall into a few buckets.

1) Auth (401/403)
- Re-create a key (takes ~10 seconds): {{api_key_create_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E2_first_success_{{variant}}
- Make sure you’re using the key for the right workspace/project

2) Model selection (404 / invalid model)
- Open the model catalog in Console and copy the model ID:
https://console.redwoodinference.com/models?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E2_first_success_{{variant}}

3) Timeouts / slow first run
- Start small: set max_tokens=64 and try streaming

Known-good “hello inference” snippets
- Curl + minimal JSON: {{quickstart_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E2_first_success_{{variant}}

Troubleshooting page (we keep this updated)
{{docs_troubleshooting_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E2_first_success_{{variant}}

CTA (primary)
- “Open troubleshooting” -> {{docs_troubleshooting_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E2_first_success_{{variant}}
CTA (secondary)
- “Try the quickstart” -> {{quickstart_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E2_first_success_{{variant}}

Optional support line (needs Support sign-off)
If you’re still blocked, reply to this email with the request_id from the error response and we’ll help you debug.

Review comments / notes
- Dev Patel: avoid promising “we’ll respond in X hours” unless we can; use “we’ll take a look”
- Tyler: ensure links go to the new console routes (we had 404 reports last week)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
EMAIL #3 — Streaming + reliability (send: +24 hours; branch based on activation)
Email ID: E3_streaming
Goal: get first_streaming_success OR reinforce best practice after first success.
Trigger (two versions):
- If activated but not streaming: first_request_success = true AND first_streaming_success = false
- If not activated: still okay to send, but copy should not assume success.

Subject line variants
- A: “Enable streaming (better UX + fewer timeouts)”
- B: “Make responses feel instant: streaming in 3 lines”

Preview text variants
- A: “Works in curl and SDKs. Example included.”
- B: “Stream tokens as they’re generated—recommended for production.”

Body (v1)
Hi {{first_name}},

If you’re building anything user-facing (chat, copilots, content tools), we recommend enabling streaming early. It improves perceived latency and helps avoid long-request timeouts.

Streaming quickstart
- Streaming example (Python + TypeScript):
https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/streaming?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E3_streaming_{{variant}}

Common gotchas
- Proxies/load balancers buffering responses (enable “no buffering” settings)
- Not flushing chunks in your server framework

If you just want a known-good test:
https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstart/streaming-curl?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E3_streaming_{{variant}}

CTA (primary)
- “Add streaming” -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/streaming?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E3_streaming_{{variant}}

Review comments / notes
- Marissa: align terminology with Console nudge (“Enable streaming” step in checklist)
- Soojin: remove “recommended for production” if we can’t back it up; alternative: “common in production”

--------------------------------------------------------------------
EMAIL #4 — Cost/latency visibility + “what good looks like” (send: +72 hours)
Email ID: E4_observability
Goal: drive console engagement (dashboard_viewed) and teach unit economics levers without overwhelming.
Trigger: ideally after first_request_success OR send regardless with softer language.

Subject line variants
- A: “See your latency + cost per request (token-level)”
- B: “What’s your per-call cost? Open the dashboard”

Preview text variants
- A: “Break down tokens, latency, and errors—then optimize.”
- B: “One view for throughput, latency, and spend.”

Body (v1)
Hi {{first_name}},

Once you have a request working, the next question is usually: “What’s my latency and cost per call?”

Redwood Console shows token-level breakdowns so you can spot issues quickly (slow prompts, long outputs, retries, etc.).

Open your dashboard
{{console_dashboard_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E4_observability_{{variant}}

What to look for first (2 minutes)
- P50 vs P95 latency (do you have a long tail?)
- Output token count (is max_tokens too high?)
- Error rate and common error types

If you want a short “what good looks like” guide:
https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/latency-cost-basics?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E4_observability_{{variant}}

CTA (primary)
- “Open Console dashboard” -> {{console_dashboard_url}}?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E4_observability_{{variant}}
CTA (secondary)
- “Latency + cost basics” -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/latency-cost-basics?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E4_observability_{{variant}}

Review comments / notes
- Nadia: confirm “token-level breakdowns” is accurate for hosted self-serve accounts at default retention
- Sean: avoid implying SLOs exist for self-serve; keep it as “visibility” not guarantees

--------------------------------------------------------------------
EMAIL #5 — Next steps (billing, routes, teammates, evals) + soft conversion (send: Day 7)
Email ID: E5_next_steps
Goal: drive higher-intent milestones without hard sell.
Trigger: send to all who haven’t churned; branch based on activation state.

Subject line variants
- A: “Next: make it production-ready (routes, billing, teammates)”
- B: “Ready to scale? A few next steps in Console”

Preview text variants
- A: “Set up a route, add billing, and keep shipping.”
- B: “Recommended checklist for week 1.”

Body (v1)
Hi {{first_name}},

If you’re still evaluating Redwood, here are a few “week 1” moves that tend to make projects go smoother:

1) Add billing (avoid interruptions)
https://console.redwoodinference.com/settings/billing?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E5_next_steps_{{variant}}

2) Create a route (pin a model + control rollouts)
https://console.redwoodinference.com/routes/new?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E5_next_steps_{{variant}}

3) Invite a teammate (shared keys, cleaner handoffs)
https://console.redwoodinference.com/settings/members?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E5_next_steps_{{variant}}

4) Optional: run a tiny eval before you ship
https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/evals-quickstart?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E5_next_steps_{{variant}}

If you’re working on a regulated workload or need a private deployment, reply with a sentence about your environment (VPC/on-prem) and we’ll point you to the right options.

CTA (primary)
- “Open next steps in Console” -> https://console.redwoodinference.com/home?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=plg_onboarding_v1&utm_content=E5_next_steps_{{variant}}

Review comments / notes
- Avery: careful with “private deployment” mention; keep it as “options exist” and route to Sales when appropriate
- Soojin: “avoid interruptions” could be read as threat; alternative: “to continue testing without limits”

--------------------------------------------------------------------
Open questions (need decisions before launch)
1) Activation definition to optimize for in email sequence:
   - Option A: first_request_success (first 2xx completion) — simplest, aligns with PM debate.
   - Option B: first_streaming_success — better UX but may delay “activation” metric.
   - Current plan: optimize for first_request_success; nudge streaming as secondary.

2) Should we include benchmark proof points in emails?
   - Proposal: keep emails focused on getting started; if we mention performance, link to Ethan’s substantiation page.
   - Risk: over-claiming; Soojin prefers minimal benchmark talk in lifecycle emails.

3) Support / reply-to handling
   - If we invite replies, what inbox + SLA? (Dev/Support sign-off)

4) Localization
   - Not in scope for sprint v1. Ensure copy is easy to localize (short sentences; avoid idioms).

5) Console deep links stability
   - We’ve had route changes causing 404. Need final validation from Marissa/Eng + update before send.

QA checklist (pre-launch)
- All links include UTMs and land on correct paths (no 404; correct auth flow)
- Unsubscribe link present + working
- Dynamic tokens have fallbacks
- Mobile formatting: short paragraphs; CTA visible above fold
- Validate suppression rules: opt-outs, activated users, sales-assisted

Change log
- 2025-01-18 (Ben): Added Email #4 dashboard emphasis + simplified checklist
- 2025-01-20 (Soojin): Removed “best-in-class” language; replaced with neutral phrasing
- 2025-01-22 (Tyler): Updated UTM placeholders + standardized campaign name to plg_onboarding_v1
